2027-03-08.title: Monday of the fifth week of the Great Fast
readings: God tests Abraham: “God himself will provide the lamb”
Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ; reverence in worship
When the bridegroom is taken away, they will fast
2027-03-08.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fifth week. The week after K'piphtho Sunday, the Sunday of the healing of the bent woman.
2027-03-08.verse: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
theo: Today we begin the most solemn page of Abraham's life. “After these things God tested Abraham. He said to him, ‘Abraham!’ And he said, ‘Here I am.’” Then comes the command no father could bear to hear: “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering.” Abraham does not argue, as he argued for Sodom. He rises early, cuts the wood and walks for three days. Then the narrator slows down: “Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac, and he himself carried the fire and the knife. So the two of them walked on together.” Isaac asks the question that hangs over the whole Old Testament: “The fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” And Abraham answers with a faith larger than he knows: “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” The Letter to the Hebrews says that Abraham “considered the fact that God is able even to raise someone from the dead.”

The Church has always read this story with her eyes on Golgotha. St Melito of Sardis taught that Isaac carrying the wood up the mountain was a figure of Christ carrying his Cross, and that the ram caught in the thicket pointed to the Lamb who would be offered in our place (in substance). What Abraham was spared, the Father did not spare himself: he gave his only Son, whom he loves. In the Gospel the disciples of John and of the Pharisees ask why Jesus' disciples do not fast. Jesus answers: “You cannot make wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them, can you? The days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.” Our Great Fast lives in those days: we fast because the Bridegroom was taken away to the Cross, and we fast in hope because he will come again. And the fast is not a patch on an old garment; it is new wine that needs a new heart. St Paul gives a simple rule for the new life: “Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ.” He praises the Corinthians for keeping “the traditions just as I handed them on to you,” and asks for order and reverence when the Church gathers to pray. The customs of veiling belonged to the Corinth of his day, and many women in our Church still cover their heads in prayer as a sign of reverence; but the heart of his teaching is that “in the Lord woman is not independent of man or man independent of woman,” and “all things come from God.”

live: Begin each day this week with three words: Here I am, Lord. Then do the first duty of the day without complaint.
Choose one small, hidden fast for the rest of this week and offer it in memory of Christ's Passion.
2027-03-08.prayer: Lord God, you tested Abraham and he answered, Here I am. You did not let him lose his son, but you did not spare your own Son and gave him up for us all. Give us Abraham's trust when your ways are dark, let us walk with Christ as Isaac walked with his father, and keep our fast as the friends of the Bridegroom, until he comes again. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: On the altar of the Holy Qurbono the Lamb whom God himself provided is offered for us, once for all, and given to us as food.

quick: God tested Abraham, who answered, “Here I am,” and set out for Moriah with Isaac.
Isaac carried the wood; Abraham trusted that God himself would provide the lamb.
Jesus' disciples will fast when the Bridegroom is taken away; the new wine needs fresh wineskins.
2027-03-08.action: Begin tomorrow with the words: Here I am, Lord.
2027-03-08.question: What am I holding so tightly that I could not offer it to God?

family.explain: God asked Abraham to do something very hard. Abraham trusted God and set out with his son Isaac. Isaac carried the wood on his back, just as Jesus later carried his Cross. When Isaac asked where the lamb was, Abraham said: God himself will provide the lamb. God did provide, and for us he gave Jesus, the Lamb of God.
family.intention: We pray for families who are going through a hard test.
family.ask: Ask: “When was it hard for us to trust God, and how did he help us?”

illus: A carpenter in Kottarakkara, a widower, took his teenage son along to every job during the boy's school holidays. One morning the boy, carrying the heaviest planks up a hill to a half-built house, asked why his father always gave him the wood and kept only the small bag of tools. His father laughed and said: because the tools are sharp, and I do not want you to get hurt. Years later, when the son was himself a father, he read Genesis 22 in church and stopped at the line where Isaac carries the wood and Abraham carries the fire and the knife. He told his wife that evening that he had finally understood his father.

pm.open: Lord, here we are. Teach us to trust you as Abraham trusted you. Amen.
share: Here I am (Genesis 22:1). Am I ready to say these words to God today?
God himself will provide the lamb (Genesis 22:8). Where do I need to trust that God will provide?
Then they will fast in those days (Luke 5:35). What does my fast this Lent say about my love for Jesus?
interc: For parents who carry heavy worries for their children.
For all who are being tested in faith, health or work.
For those who are fasting this Lent, that their fast may be full of love.
For our Church, that we may keep the traditions handed on to us with reverence and joy.
For all who will be baptised or return to the sacraments this Easter.
pm.close: Father, you gave your only Son as the Lamb for our sins. Make us obedient like Abraham, patient like Isaac, and faithful in our fast until the Bridegroom returns. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Book of Genesis opens its most moving chapter: after these things God tested Abraham. God called, Abraham, and he said, Here I am (Genesis 22:1). Then God asked him to offer his only son, Isaac, whom he loved.

Abraham obeyed without understanding. He laid the wood on Isaac's shoulders and carried the fire and the knife himself, and the two of them walked on together (Genesis 22:6). Isaac asked: where is the lamb? Abraham said: God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son (Genesis 22:8). The Fathers saw here Christ carrying the wood of the Cross up the hill of Calvary.

In the Gospel Jesus says that the wedding guests cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, but the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast (Luke 5:34–35). We are in those days. We fast because our Bridegroom was taken from us to the Cross, and we fast in hope because he is risen and will return.

St Paul says: be imitators of me, as I am of Christ (1 Corinthians 11:1). Abraham's trust, Isaac's patience and Paul's example all point to Jesus. In these last weeks of the Fast, let us say each morning: Here I am, Lord. God himself will provide. Amen.
kids: Children, God asked Abraham to do something very hard, and Abraham trusted him. Isaac carried the wood up the mountain, just like Jesus carried his Cross. When Isaac asked, where is the lamb?, his father said: God will give the lamb. God gave us Jesus, the Lamb of God. Tomorrow when you wake up, say: Here I am, Jesus!

sub: Father and son walk on together.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
